cognitive_validation.rationale: The mechanization is presented with a coherent, systematic, nonsupernatural economic and mechanical logic (cost of running engines, hand-winch labor, steam trawler operation). However coherence alone does not make a novum.

novum_candidates.description: The petrol/motor engines and steam winch that Captain Joshua experimentally installed (and removed) on the sailing trawler I'll Try, representing mechanization of traditional Brixham fishing craft.
novum_candidates.estrangement_rationale: No cognitive estrangement is produced; the story is a mundane realist maritime tragedy set in a recognizable Brixham fishing economy. There is no departure from the empirical norm requiring a fictional novum to explain.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: While the failed motor experiment sets up the financial hardship, the narrative logic is governed by the storm, human endurance, and religious faith rather than by any novum-driven world change. The technology is an incidental realistic device, not the overriding narrative logic.

novelty.rationale: Petrol motors, steam winches, and steam trawlers (the Williwaw) are all part of the ordinary early-twentieth-century empirical world of the story. They constitute no totalizing or world-altering difference from the authorial/implied empirical norm; they are period-realistic technology, not an estranging novum.
